headline: Berry merger lifts profit sharply, EPS dips on dilution
summary_short: Amcor's first full quarter fully consolidating Berry Global saw net sales rise 71% y/y to $5,745M and net income rise 37% to $262M, but diluted EPS fell 14% to $0.113 as diluted shares outstanding grew 60% from merger-related issuance.
summary_long: Net sales rose 71% y/y to $5,745M, almost entirely from the April 2025 Berry Global merger (~$2,363M) and favorable FX, partly offset by a 2% organic decline on lower volumes. Gross margin held roughly flat at 19.6%; operating margin fell to 8.0% from 9.3% as merger-related SG&A, intangible amortization, and restructuring/integration costs outpaced gross-profit growth. Net income rose 37% to $262M, but diluted EPS fell 14% to $0.113 as diluted shares grew 60% from Berry-related issuance. Cash was $825M, flat q/q, up from $432M a year ago. Segment Adjusted EBIT: Flexible $426M (+29%), Rigid $295M (+377%). No revenue/EPS outlook was given; the company reaffirmed Berry Plan synergy targets and gave FY2026 restructuring cash-spend guidance.

drivers.explanation: Results reflect the first full quarter consolidating Berry Global following the April 30, 2025 merger; management reaffirmed its Berry Plan target of ~$530M cumulative pre-tax synergies by fiscal 2028 and continued integration/restructuring spend.
The Merger added approximately $2,363M of net sales and FX added ~$110M; excluding these, underlying sales fell ~2% on lower volumes, partly offset by favorable price/mix.
MD&A states gross margin "remained stable" y/y at 19.6% as merger-added revenue and synergies offset cost pressure.
Compression driven by merger-related SG&A (+$159M), acquired-intangible amortization (+$94M), and restructuring/transaction/integration costs (+$69M) growing faster than gross profit.

Growth driven by higher gross profit (+$465M) and other income (+$24M), partly offset by higher SG&A, amortization, restructuring costs, and interest expense (+$78M), all primarily attributed to the Merger.
EPS fell despite net income available to ordinary shareholders rising 38% because diluted weighted-average shares grew 60% y/y from Berry merger share issuance.
